elements.title: Evidence for multi-Li+ clustering in lithium-ion battery electrolytes (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Evidence for multi-Li+ clustering in lithium-ion battery electrolytes

Machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations, spectroscopy, electrochemical data and quantum-chemical calculations reveal previously unstudied multi-lithium-ion complexes without bound anions, improving understanding of lithium-ion-battery functionality at the atomic level.

  • James M. Stevenson
  • Garvit Agarwal
  • Richard A. Friesner
ArticleOpen Access14 Oct 2026

elements.title: Global conservation area coverage substantially exceeds current estimates (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Global conservation area coverage substantially exceeds current estimates

A globally representative sample of 25 countries and territories indicates that conservation areas cover 26.81% of the land, much closer to the 30% by 2030 target than officially reported.

  • Helen M. K. O’Neill
  • Joe Beeken
  • Robert J. Smith
ArticleOpen Access14 Oct 2026

elements.title: Engineered TYK2 dependence enables myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonism (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Engineered TYK2 dependence enables myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonism

A tetravalent nanobody-based myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonist recapitulates IL-10’s potent suppression of monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells while avoiding stimulation of T cells.

  • D. Alejandro Canaria
  • Trang T. T. Nguyen
  • Tangsheng Yi
ArticleOpen Access14 Oct 2026

elements.title: Elp1 is required for myeloid differentiation and brain repopulation (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Elp1 is required for myeloid differentiation and brain repopulation

Primary cultured haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells are used to analyse the molecular mechanisms of brain myeloid differentiation, and this platform enabled the identification of elongation factor ELP1 as an important regulator of this process.

  • Marius Marc-Daniel Mader
  • Wanhua Li
  • Marius Wernig
Article14 Oct 2026

elements.title: Modelling mouse embryogenesis from chemically induced totipotent stem cells (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Modelling mouse embryogenesis from chemically induced totipotent stem cells

A mouse embryo model derived from chemically induced totipotent-like stem cells progresses through key developmental milestones, including gastrulation, embryonic axis formation, haematopoiesis and early organogenesis.

  • Hua Wu
  • Yanyan Hu
  • Sheng Ding
Article14 Oct 2026

elements.title: Competing mechanisms toughen bcc binary and medium-entropy alloys at 20 K (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Competing mechanisms toughen bcc binary and medium-entropy alloys at 20 K

The mechanical properties of medium-entropy alloys at 20 K show a plateau in tensile yield strength and fracture toughness as a function of temperature, with no apparent ductile-to-brittle transition.

  • David H. Cook
  • Xiaoyu Chen
  • Robert O. Ritchie
ArticleOpen Access14 Oct 2026

elements.title: Parity-dependent coupling of molecular spin chains to a superconductor (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Parity-dependent coupling of molecular spin chains to a superconductor

Scanning tunnelling spectroscopy shows that the fractional spin-1/2 end states of molecular Haldane chains couple differently to a superconducting condensate depending on whether the chain contains an even or odd number of spin-1 triangulene units.

  • Katerina Vaxevani
  • Jon Ortuzar
  • Jose Ignacio Pascual
Article14 Oct 2026

elements.title: Capillary-selective vasodilation through myosin inhibition halts ischaemic cascades (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Capillary-selective vasodilation through myosin inhibition halts ischaemic cascades

R(+)2501 reverses capillary no-reflow by relaxing pericytes, restoring microvascular perfusion and improving survival in animal models of myocardial infarction and acute kidney injury.

  • Máté Pénzes
  • Máté Winternitz
  • András Málnási-Csizmadia
Article14 Oct 2026

elements.contents:

A year-long single-blind study shows that multiple satellites can accurately detect and quantify methane point-source emissions.

  • Frances E. Reuland
  • Taylor Adams
  • Adam R. Brandt
Article14 Oct 2026

elements.title: De novo design of cysteine proteases (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
De novo design of cysteine proteases

De novo-designed enzymes use an activated cysteine nucleophile to hydrolyse polypeptide backbones in a sequence-dependent manner.

  • Hojae Choi
  • Magnus S. Bauer
  • David Baker
Article14 Oct 2026

elements.title: Computational design of metalloproteases (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Computational design of metalloproteases

RFdiffusion methods are used to de novo design proteins with water-activating zinc-based active sites adjacent to a peptide substrate binding pocket, yielding highly active, programmable proteases with potential applications in therapeutics, biotechnology and bioremediation.

  • Anqi Chen
  • Kejia Wu
  • David Baker
Article14 Oct 2026

elements.title: Divergent genomic evolution in astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Divergent genomic evolution in astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas

Longitudinal genomic analyses in patients with astrocytoma or oligodendrioglioma suggest that these two types of tumour differ in the mechanisms by which they become resistant to treatment, with astrocytomas accumulating copy-number alterations and chromosomal instability markers but oligodendrogliomas acquiring new driver mutations.

  • Tamrin Chowdhury
  • C. Mircea S. Tesileanu
  • Do-Hyun Nam
ArticleOpen Access14 Oct 2026

elements.title: Rh3+ stabilized in KRh@MFI catalyses regioselective hydroformylation (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Rh3+ stabilized in KRh@MFI catalyses regioselective hydroformylation

DFT investigations combined with spectroscopic and catalytic studies of disrupted subnanometric Rh2O3 clusters show that Rh+ centres in a zeolite-based catalyst are blocked with N-containing molecules, whereas Rh3+ sites are stabilized, allowing hydroformylation reactions with enhanced regioselectivity and efficiency.

  • Minjie Zhao
  • Reisel Millán
  • Avelino Corma
Article14 Oct 2026

elements.title: Targeted stimulation of motor cortex ensembles drives learned movements (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Targeted stimulation of motor cortex ensembles drives learned movements

Optogenetic stimulation of motor-cortex neuron ensembles shows that precisely timed activity in the primary motor cortex can generate learned neural patterns and movements, demonstrating an active role in skilled motor control.

  • Qiyu Chen
  • An Wu
  • Takaki Komiyama
Article14 Oct 2026

elements.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat

Artificial intelligence-enabled quantification and analyses of brown adipose tissue (BAT) activity uncover links between BAT and a healthier metabolic profile along with lower rates of psychiatric disease, and can identify pharmacologic agents that could be repurposed to activate this tissue in humans.

  • Nicolás Gómez-Banoy
  • Jorge A. Barrero
  • Paul Cohen
ArticleOpen Access14 Oct 2026

elements.title: Early tetrapod neck mobility modelled using an extant analogue (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Early tetrapod neck mobility modelled using an extant analogue

Biomechanical analysis of several early tetrapods using sturgeon as an analogue revealed that early tetrapods had limited neck mobility despite separation of the head and shoulders.

  • Dana E. Korneisel
  • Cassandra M. Donatelli
  • Hillary C. Maddin
ArticleOpen Access14 Oct 2026

elements.title: Intrinsic physicochemical activity at microplastic–water interfaces (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Intrinsic physicochemical activity at microplastic–water interfaces

Commodity microplastics exhibit intrinsic physicochemical activity at water interfaces, manifested by spontaneous generation of reactive oxygen species, challenging the prevailing paradigm of plastic inertness, with implications for human health and the environment.

  • Naixin Qian
  • Ruoqi Zhao
  • Wei Min
ArticleOpen Access14 Oct 2026

elements.title: Hidden reaction pathways inform additive engineering for perovskite LEDs (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Hidden reaction pathways inform additive engineering for perovskite LEDs

Resolution and control of the hidden solution-phase chemistry of 5-aminovaleric acid added to perovskite precursor solutions is described for producing films with a near-unity mean peak photoluminescence quantum yield and near-infrared perovskite LEDs with enhanced external quantum efficiencies.

  • Sung-Doo Baek
  • Yu-Ting Yang
  • Letian Dou
Article14 Oct 2026
